clue.text: A composer to beat the Twist?

explanation.surface: A musical question about which composer could outdo a famous dance craze.
explanation.walkthrough: The Twist looks like the 1960s dance, but here it is a twist in thread: to ravel is to tangle, to twist up worse than a twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was a French composer; as a verb, ravel means to tangle threads, outdoing a mere twist.

clue.text: Caught everyone after bread -how to find out if they are here

definitions.text: how to find out if they are here

indicators.note: after tells us the caught-everyone pair comes behind the bread

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Someone catches the whole group after handing out bread, then wonders who is present.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading out the names on a register is the classic way to check attendance.

clue.text: Such meat should come with the product of vine, my boy!

indicators.note: a product is something made out of raw material, so these letters are worked into something new

parts.note: a father's boy is his son

explanation.surface: A host recommends serving a particular meat with wine, addressing his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The product of vine' suggests wine, but 'product of' is the anagram signal working on the word vine itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer meat is the kind of meat in question.

clue.text: Look, a decoration for working in yarns

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone points out an ornament suitable for knitting or weaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A weaving frame is the apparatus on which yarns are worked into cloth.

clue.text: 20 can never be put in an inescapable position

definitions.text: 20 can never be put in an inescapable position

parts.words: 20 can never be put in an inescapable position
parts.note: 20 is a round building, which has no angles, so nobody could trap it in one; the plain sense is being trapped with no way out

explanation.surface: A claim that some round thing can never be trapped with no escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to the answer ROTUNDA, a circular building: having no angles, it cannot be trapped in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being trapped where there is no way out is being backed into an angle of the room.

clue.text: All sorts of events from ten to eleven for a bird whose dead on time from the sound of it?

definitions.text: All sorts of events from ten to eleven

indicators.note: the solver is told to say the bird phrase out loud and hear another phrase

parts.words: a bird whose dead on time
parts.note: a single crow that has died on the hour

explanation.surface: A whimsical puzzle about a busy hour and a bird that dies punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: From ten to eleven is one hour packed with events; 'one crow dead (on the) hour' said quickly sounds like the answer, a phrase from a poem by Thomas Mordaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour packed with many happenings is a busy, eventful single hour.

clue.text: Close to being stingy

explanation.definitionFit: Near means nearby in distance, and also tight-fisted with money in older usage.

clue.text: The transport one is always delighted with

definitions.text: The transport one is always delighted with

parts.words: The transport one is always delighted with
parts.note: transport here is an emotional transport, being carried away with joy, not a vehicle

explanation.surface: A question about which mode of travel always pleases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' suggests buses and trains, but a transport of delight is ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic joy is the state of being carried away, a transport of the emotions.

clue.text: Terror of the old man when King Edward turned in

indicators.note: in tells us the turned royal pair goes inside the father

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, dad

indicators.note: turned means the royal letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Edwardus Rex, is King Edward's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A father's fright when the king turned up inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the king's cipher and 'in' places it inside the father; 'King Edward' also tempts as a potato variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Great fear and terror are synonyms.

clue.text: United Nations may be transformed? Not in any other language

parts.note: something that can be converted into another form is capable of being rendered differently

explanation.surface: A remark that UN documents may be altered, yet cannot exist in other tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be transformed' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a definition of the word meaning able to be converted.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase impossible to render in a foreign tongue has no equivalent elsewhere.

clue.text: A bit of drill in Col North's green cloth

indicators.note: a bit of means only part of the following words is used, here a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Part of an army colonel's drill uniform made of green fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'drilL IN COL North'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln green is the traditional green woollen fabric associated with Robin Hood.

clue.text: It's no longer enough to show what others should do

definitions.text: to show what others should do

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in place
ample means plentiful, enough

explanation.surface: A suggestion that something once sufficient now must serve as a lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A model held up for imitation shows others how to behave.

clue.text: Weapon provided by company on the quiet

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A firm discreetly supplies a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosh is a short heavy club, a blunt instrument used to strike.

clue.text: Right tour about a Cornish town

indicators.note: about can mean around in a jumbled way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suitable tour around a town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is the cathedral city and county town of Cornwall, in south-west England.

clue.text: Supply amusement to a large number

parts.note: fun means amusement
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Providing entertainment for a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a reserve or stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A fund is a stock or reserve of money or resources.

clue.text: Push forward in footwear, size five

indicators.note: in tells us the number goes inside the footwear

parts.note: a shoe is an item of footwear
five in Roman numerals is V, like a shoe size

explanation.surface: Trying on a pair of size five shoes in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To shove is to push roughly forward.

clue.text: A position that's secure only if everyone's behind you

definitions.text: A position that's secure only if everyone's behind you

parts.words: A position that's secure only if everyone's behind you
parts.note: being ahead of everyone means the whole field trails you; the surface hints at support from followers

explanation.surface: A leader's position depends on everyone backing him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind you' sounds like support, but it means literally following you in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading place in a race or ranking has every other competitor behind.

clue.text: No stenographer can pen such ordinary letters

definitions.text: No stenographer can pen such ordinary letters

parts.words: No stenographer can pen such ordinary letters
parts.note: a shorthand typist uses special symbols, while this person writes ordinary letters in full

explanation.surface: A complaint that shorthand typists cannot write ordinary correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests correspondence, but it means the ordinary alphabet as opposed to shorthand signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes words out in full by hand, not in shorthand symbols.

clue.text: The mob he manipulated was like a wild beast

indicators.note: manipulated means handled and rearranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A crowd stirred up by an agitator behaves like an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is a huge monstrous creature, from the Book of Job.

clue.text: Yarn the stay-at-home couldn't account for

definitions.text: Yarn the stay-at-home couldn't account for

parts.words: Yarn the stay-at-home couldn't account for
parts.note: a story told by someone back from abroad, which a person who never goes away cannot check

explanation.surface: Someone who never leaves home cannot explain a strange story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' could be thread for knitting, but here it is a story, and a tall one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story told by someone returning from far places, hard to verify.

clue.text: A suitable building for a circular letter?

definitions.text: A suitable building for a circular letter?

parts.words: A suitable building for a circular letter?
parts.note: a round building would suit the round letter O; the surface suggests a circular sent by post

explanation.surface: A question about where mass-mailed letters should be kept.
explanation.walkthrough: A circular letter is a mass mailing, but here it is the round letter O; the answer also splits as ROTUND (circular) and A (a letter).
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, often domed, fitting something round.

clue.text: One inclined to feel sick on the wing

definitions.text: One inclined to feel sick on the wing

parts.words: One inclined to feel sick on the wing
parts.note: the hinged flap tilts up and down on an aircraft wing; the surface describes an airsick passenger

explanation.surface: A nervous flyer who gets airsick.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is an airsick traveller; the answer is a hinged flap that tilts on a wing, and it splits as AILER (one inclined to ail) + ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a movable hinged flap on an aircraft wing that tilts to bank the plane.

clue.text: … being one with no foundation.

parts.note: a story with no basis in fact; the dots carry on from the previous clue

explanation.surface: Continuing a thought about something lacking any base.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues the clue before; read alone, a tale with no basis in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend or false belief that has no factual basis.

clue.text: Silent afterthought; glands too swollen to speak?

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: Someone stays quiet with a final thought because their throat is too swollen.
explanation.definitionFit: This illness swells the salivary glands, making talking painful.

clue.text: Longing to take an unknown number 'from scratch

parts.note: an itch is what makes you scratch
Y is an algebra symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Wanting to work out a number from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from scratch' suggests starting from nothing; here 'scratch' gives ITCH, and Y, an algebraic unknown, is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless desire, as in itchy feet, is longing.

clue.text: Dumpy Oxbridge sportsman?

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is being down in the dumps; a sportsman who represents Oxford or Cambridge earns a blue.

clue.text: A science graduate developed into a scoundrel

indicators.note: developed means changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree

explanation.surface: A science graduate who turned into a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a strikebreaker, and by extension a contemptible rogue.

clue.text: Act in 51 pieces or only one, widely admired?

indicators.note: in tells us the act goes inside the two broken-up numerals

parts.note: 51 broken into 1 and 50 gives the Roman numerals I and L
to do is to act

explanation.surface: A performer acting in many scenes, or just one, and still popular.
explanation.walkthrough: '5l' is 51 misread; split into pieces it is 1 and 50, I and L, with DO inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a single figure adored by many fans.

clue.text: Conveyance for a little Citizens' Advice Bureau

parts.note: mini means small, little
CAB is the abbreviation for Citizens' Advice Bureau, a British free advice charity

explanation.surface: A ride for a small local advice office.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicab is a hired car booked by phone, a vehicle for passengers in Britain.

clue.text: Suffer emigrants' leader to break fresh ground

indicators.note: to break means the leading letter splits the jumbled ground
fresh means renewed, so the letters of ground are rearranged
leader means the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Emigrants endure hardship as their leader breaks new ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges GROUND into UNDRGO and 'to break' puts E, the leader of 'emigrants', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or endure it.

clue.text: Hush! Blame's freshly laid on the slaughterhouse

parts.note: sh means hush

indicators.note: freshly means anew, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A demand for quiet as blame is heaped on the abattoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly' rearranges the six letters of 'Blame's', the 's counting as a letter; 'laid on' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambles was once the name for a meat market or abattoir, hence any scene of carnage.

clue.text: Light meal for pound, French one, cold and hot

parts.note: L stands for pound, from Latin libra
un is French for one
C stands for cold on taps
H stands for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A recipe for a simple midday meal served both cold and hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal is usually lighter than dinner.
